items.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the six characteristics of life?
items.explanation: Having a backbone is NOT a characteristic of life, many living things like worms, insects, and plants have no backbone at all!

items.stem: A sunflower turns its face to follow sunlight throughout the day. Which characteristic of life does this demonstrate?
items.explanation: Turning toward light (phototropism) is a response to a stimulus, the stimulus is light!

items.stem: Your body shivers when you're cold and sweats when you're hot. This is an example of:
items.explanation: Shivering and sweating are ways your body regulates its internal temperature, that's homeostasis in action!

items.stem: Which characteristic of life requires that ALL living things (from bacteria to blue whales) have at least one cell?
items.explanation: Cell Theory states that all living things are made of cells. This is characteristic #1, no exceptions!

items.stem: A fire can grow, consume oxygen, and release energy. Is a fire alive? Why or why not?

options.text: No, it cannot reproduce or maintain homeostasis
Yes, it uses energy and grows
Yes, it responds to oxygen as a stimulus
No, it is not made of cells, but otherwise qualifies

items.explanation: Fire fails multiple characteristics: it cannot reproduce, is not made of cells, and doesn't maintain homeostasis. ALL six must be met to be considered alive.

items.stem: What is the main reason viruses are usually classified as nonliving?

options.text: They evolve too slowly to be considered alive
They are too small to be seen under most microscopes
They have no cells of their own

items.explanation: Most scientists classify viruses as nonliving because the cell is the minimum unit of life. Viruses have no cells of their own, so they cannot carry out life processes independently.

items.stem: Bacteria consist of a single cell. This makes them:
items.explanation: Unicellular means one cell. Bacteria are single-celled (unicellular) organisms, and they are prokaryotic, not eukaryotic.

items.stem: In prokaryotic cells, where is the DNA found?
items.explanation: Prokaryotic cells do NOT have a nucleus, their DNA floats freely in the cytoplasm.

items.stem: Can a unicellular organism also be eukaryotic?

options.text: Yes, for example, amoeba and paramecium are unicellular eukaryotes
No, all unicellular organisms are prokaryotic
No, eukaryotes must always be multicellular
Yes, but only if they have a cell wall

items.explanation: Unicellular and eukaryotic are not mutually exclusive! Amoeba, paramecium, and many protists are single-celled but still have a nucleus, making them unicellular eukaryotes.

items.stem: A student looks at a cell under a microscope and sees no nucleus, the DNA appears to be floating freely in the cell. What type of cell is this?

options.text: Eukaryotic, it must have lost its nucleus
Prokaryotic, no nucleus is the defining feature
Multicellular, large cells don't always have nuclei
Unicellular, small cells never have nuclei

items.explanation: The absence of a membrane-bound nucleus is the defining feature of prokaryotic cells. Eukaryotic cells always have a nucleus enclosing their DNA.
